label: Bible Study
prompt: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a _____ treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:
verse: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:
note: In 1611 English 'peculiar' meant 'one's own' — God calling Israel his treasured possession, not his oddballs.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their _____; and their works do follow them.
verse: And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.
note: A gentle promise for those who die in the Lord: rest from their labours, and their good works follow.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning _____, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
verse: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
note: 'Cunning' here means skillful — Esau the outdoorsman, Jacob the homebody, and trouble brewing in the tents.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be _____.
verse: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
note: The Preacher's prayer advice: God is in heaven and you are on earth, so keep it brief.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Nay but, O man, who art thou that _____ against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?
verse: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?
note: Paul's potter-and-clay rebuke — 'who art thou that repliest against God?' — echoes Isaiah 45:9.
